conceptual assets.information: A software-visible system-information word initialized to the configured clock frequency and replaceable by a bus write; the module's readback behavior depends on this value.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because bus_req_i.data can overwrite the held system-information value on line 95 when the access condition on line 94 is met, allowing a false value to be reported.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker able to issue a qualifying bus write can replace the reported frequency with a false value at line 95, causing software or an integrator to rely on incorrect system information.

considered, not kept.reason: The build-time-values rule bars the generic- and constant-derived memory, cache, boot and peripheral configuration from being conceptual assets because no runtime element changes it, despite its assignments on lines 102-150.

The access-command-fields rule treats bus_req_i.stb, bus_req_i.rw and bus_req_i.addr as parts of the access rather than independent information; they only select and qualify the sysinfo access on lines 94 and 161-162.

buf_adr is only a registered copy of the access address used while serving the transfer, so the held-address rule makes it part of the access rather than a separate piece of information on lines 158, 162 and 168.

considered, not kept.concept: Bus response handshake and error status
considered, not kept.reason: The acknowledge only repeats the request strobe and the error is tied to a constant, so bus-handshake-copy and constant-status rules bar them as independent information on lines 160 and 169-170.
The clocks-and-resets rule excludes clk_i and rstn_i from conceptual assets under all questions; they only time or reset the logic on lines 58-59 and 89-93.

reply keys: the 2026-10-13 format as written in 'raw'; 'reply' holds it in v5 keys
